Hi all — did a first legal review overnight. High-level notes and proposed actions below. I’ve kept things terse to help procurement/GCs move quickly.

1) SCCs / Annex B: Redwood is generally fine adopting the EU SCCs framework. Two asks: 
   - We will propose the standard controller-processor SCCs with a supplementary Annex describing the subprocessor approval process (30-day notice + right to object).
   - For transfers to research/externally hosted inference endpoints (where telemetry may be analyzed outside EU), we propose a TIA that documents safeguards (encryption in transit, access controls, retention limits).

2) DPA redlines: Main items to reconcile with Aureus markups:
   - Data categories: we need to explicitly exclude model weights as ‘derived/operational artifacts’ that Redwood treats as system assets (we do not persist customer PII in model weights by default).
   - Incident notification SLA: Aureus requests 12-hour notification — we should propose 24 hours for incidents impacting model outputs and 72 hours for general data events unless regulatory trigger requires shorter.
   - Subprocessor list: request Aureus accepts a rights-managed monthly list and an approval window for any new critical subprocessor (7 business days).

3) TIA (owner: Marissa) — please produce:
   - One-page flow diagram + bullet summary (where data originates, transient storage, inference endpoints, telemetry destinations, and jurisdiction hops).
   - Short list of technical safeguards (encryption, IAM, audit logs) and retention defaults.

4) Order form residency language: suggest a simple clause tying residency to the deployment mode: Hosted = best-effort region pinning; Dedicated = customer-pinned region + guaranteed residency for inputs and logs. We should identify any features that still require cross-border processing and surface them in the TIA.

Next steps / ETA: legal pass complete with tracked changes by close of day Wednesday (2026-06-17). Marissa — can you target an initial TIA draft by EOD Tuesday? Samantha / Aureus — if you can confirm they accept the SCCs framework with the proposed subprocessor notice approach, that will speed sign-off.

Laura Bennett
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Thanks Ben / Laura — appreciate the quick turnaround. Aureus is generally comfortable with adopting the SCCs framework plus the subprocessor notice language you proposed. Two small asks before we sign: 

- Could you adopt the 24-hour incident notification for incidents that materially impact data subjects, and commit to expedited regulatory notification support if required? (Aureus legal will accept 24 hours for material incidents.)
- Please include a one-paragraph summary of model-weight handling in the DPA (we need explicit wording that model weights are not used to store customer PII and details on retraining safeguards).

If Marissa can share the TIA by EOD Tuesday that covers the flows and the small feature list that may cross borders, we can push to signature the following week.

Appreciate the clear owners — will loop in our DPO if any of these items need deeper technical detail.

Best,
